逐字稿（889 字）

A Good morning, and welcome to Riverside City Library. How can I help you today?

B Hi, good morning. Um, I've just started at the university, and I'd like to join the library, please. A friend told me it's quite easy to sign up, so I thought I would come in on my way to my first lecture.

A It is, yes. It only takes a few minutes. I just need to go through this application form with you, and then we can get your card ready for you. Is that all right?

B Yes, that's fine. I'm in no rush this morning, because my lecture doesn't start until eleven, so please take your time.

A Wonderful. Let's start with the basics, then. Could I have your family name, please?

B Sure. q01It's Hargreaves. That's H-A-R-G-R-E-A-V-E-S. A lot of people leave out the second R, so I always spell it out.

A Thank you, Hargreaves, I'll be careful with that one. Now, I also need your date of birth for our records, if you don't mind.

B Oh, of course. It's the 13th of March, no, sorry, I always do that. q02It's the 14th of March. I think I mix it up because my sister was born on the thirteenth, just one year before me.

A That's easy to do when you share a birthday month. The 14th of March, then. You must be a first-year student, I imagine. Have you lived in the city for long?

B Not at all, I only arrived last week. Well, I'm renting a room in a shared house near the campus, and honestly I'm still getting used to finding my way around, especially when it comes to the buses.

A It does take a while. Everybody tells me the bus routes are the hardest part of moving here. Right, so what's the house number where you're staying?

B q03It's number 15. Not 50, which is what people often think, because the numbers on that road jump around in a very confusing way, and the postman gets it wrong almost every week.

A Fifteen, okay, I've got that. And is that a long road? I'd like to know the name of the street, of course, for the form.

B Oh, yes, sorry. q04It's Harlow Road. That's H-A-R-L-O-W, and then Road, like the normal word. It's quite short, really, and it's only a few minutes' walk from the main entrance of the university.

A I know it, it's close to the main bus stop, isn't it? I think that line goes straight into the town centre, which must be very convenient for you.

B Yes, exactly, it's really convenient. Anyway, I should mention that I have my student card with me, if you need the number from it. I know that some libraries ask for it.

A Yes, please, we ask for that from all of our students, so that we can check your enrolment. Could you read it out for me?

B Of course. Let me find it in my bag. Yes, here it is. It's 3417, and it's printed on the front, just below my photograph.

A Sorry, was that 3470? The print on those cards is sometimes very small, and I can never read the last two numbers.

B q05No, it's 3417. Thirty-four, seventeen, if that helps. The last two numbers are the ones that always give people trouble.

A Got it, thank you very much. Now, I'm curious, and the form asks as well. What are you studying at the university?

B q06I'm doing a degree in civil engineering. It's quite a practical course, so I spend a lot of time in the labs and not many hours in the library, which is the reason I've been slow to join.

A Well, we have a good section on engineering, so I'm sure you'll find plenty of useful books. Your card will be ready in a couple of days, so which day would be best for you to come and collect it?

B Well, Wednesday would be good, oh, wait, I have a lab session then. q07Let's say Thursday instead. I'm usually free in the afternoons on Thursdays, so that works well.

A Thursday, no problem at all. We have three branches in the city, so which one would you like to use most often? The central one, or one of the others?

B Hmm, the Central branch is the biggest, I know, but it's quite far from my house. q08I think the Eastside branch is much closer, so I'll choose that one, and I'll visit the big one only when I need a special book.

A That sounds like a sensible choice. Now, we like to know what our members enjoy reading, so that we can order new books. Do you have a favourite subject?

B q09Yes, I love history, especially the history of cities and their buildings. I've read quite a lot about that already, and I'd like to find more books about the old part of this city.

A Wonderful, we have a whole floor for that. Finally, how would you like us to contact you about reservations and overdue books? We can send a letter, call you, or write to you.

B q10Email is best for me. I never answer my phone when I'm studying, and letters tend to get lost in the shared house, so email is much safer.

A Perfect. That's everything I need. Thank you very much, and enjoy the library.

B Thanks a lot. Goodbye.
